issues.description: The problem statement/UML require that each class has a public constructor that takes all attributes in the UML order (Ride must have a constructor taking (String name, char abbreviation)). However, the solution's Ride class defines a constructor public Ride(String name) that does not accept the abbreviation and instead sets a default 'A'. This contradicts the specification and will confuse students and break the expected subclass constructor chaining (subclasses are expected to call super(name, abbreviation)).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Ride constructor match the UML/instructions by providing a public Ride(String name, char abbreviation) constructor that assigns both attributes. Update the solution (and template if present) so subclasses call super(name, abbreviation). Ensure all subclass constructors accept superclass attributes first (name, abbreviation) per the UML.
